explanations: terra: After Adam tells the names, God says He knows what the angels reveal and what they conceal, coupling speech with the visible-hidden distinction.

luna: The section’s water-in-milk dictionary image describes something present but obscured through mixture. This verse forbids mixing truth with falsehood and concealing truth, showing the moral cost of a mixture that hides what is true. | terra: Mixing truth with falsehood and then concealing it makes disclosed truth disappear within another substance, close to the section's water-in-milk figure.
terra: After a killing was concealed, God is مُخْرِجٌ what the people were hiding, a precise instance of the covered fact being brought into view.
terra: Hearts become hard after the signs, even harder than stone, reversing the section's account of admonition polishing and opening hearts.
terra: The speakers ask why their companions تُحَدِّثُونَهُم with what God has disclosed to them, explicitly coupling telling with an opening of concealed knowledge.

luna: The source section includes the orphan and the petitioner among the surah’s surrounding acts of care. This covenant likewise joins kindness to orphans with speaking well to people, including the way one addresses the vulnerable.
terra: Gabriel brings the Quran down upon the Prophet's heart as confirmation and guidance, a precise revealed-speech-to-guided-heart sequence.

luna: The source section names “losing the way” as the root’s familiar sense. This verse says a person has ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ, a specific departure from the middle path that preserves the root’s path sense beside its hiddenness sense.
terra: Whatever good people send ahead they will find with God, treating unseen preserved action as something later encountered.

luna: The section says the favor will no longer remain under cover but be told. This verse condemns concealing clear proofs and guidance after they have been made clear, a direct reversal of disclosure. | terra: Those who conceal clear proofs and guidance after God has made them clear reverse the section's movement from found guidance into telling.
luna: The following verse describes those who repent, repair, and make clear what was concealed. It completes 2:159 with the return from hiddenness to explicit explanation.
terra: Those who conceal what God sent down in the Book sell disclosure for gain, the opposite stance to speaking openly of divine gift.

luna: The section cites deniers who ask how people can be created anew after disappearing into the earth. This verse stages a person’s death for a century and return to life, with his food and drink preserved and his donkey restored, as a concrete answer to that denial.

luna: The section reports denial of resurrection after bodily disappearance. Abraham asks how God gives life to the dead, and is shown birds gathered back after being placed on separate hills, a specific reversal of disintegration.

luna: The section says the Lord’s favor should be spoken openly. This verse says open charity is good while concealing it and giving it to the poor is better, setting a specific boundary on when a gift is shown. | terra: The ayah directly compares making charity visible with concealing it while giving to the poor, a concrete moral use of open and covered action.

luna: The section imagines someone hidden in a crowd and found at a glance. This verse describes needy people who appear self-sufficient but are recognized by their marks, making concealed need perceptible without an insistent request.

luna: The section moves from night and day to telling the Lord’s favor. This verse joins night and day with giving both secretly and publicly, a concrete parallel between hidden and open acts of generosity.

luna: The source section labels ض ل ل branch B004 with the dictionary sense “forget.” This witness rule uses أَن تَضِلَّ for a woman’s lapse of memory and pairs it with a second witness’s reminder, so what slips from memory is restored by speech. | terra: The witness may تَضِلَّ, here forget, and another witness restores what vanished from memory by speaking; this is the section's exact forgetfulness sense of the root.
terra: Whether people reveal what is within themselves or conceal it, God calls it to account, giving inward hiddenness a future public consequence.
luna: The section connects disappearance with forgetting and gives 2:282 as its example. This prayer asks not to be held accountable if people forget or err, making forgetfulness a named human limit.
terra: The Prophet is told to say that God knows what people hide in their breasts and what they reveal, placing the visible-hidden pair in proclamation.
terra: Every soul تَجِدُ its good and evil deeds present, giving intellectual and moral finding an unveiled final form.

luna: The source section describes finding by perception and the later telling of a favor. Zakariya repeatedly وَجَدَ provisions with Mary, asks where they came from, and she answers that they are from Allah; discovery leads to attribution. | terra: Zechariah repeatedly finds provision with Mary and asks its source; her answer attributes the unexpectedly found gift to God.
terra: The story is news of the unseen revealed to the Prophet, who was not present when the lots were cast or the dispute occurred.

luna: This verse repeats the warning not to clothe truth with falsehood or conceal it. It is a second direct formulation of the mixture-and-hiddenness relation in 2:42. | terra: The People of the Book are charged with clothing truth in falsehood and knowingly concealing it, repeating the image of discernible truth covered by mixture.
terra: The believers are commanded to remember God's favor when He joined once-hostile hearts, a specific hidden transformation recounted as blessing.
terra: Hatred has appeared from opponents' mouths while what their breasts conceal is greater, sharply separating audible disclosure from a deeper hidden interior.
terra: People say with their mouths what is not in their hearts, while God knows what they conceal; spoken appearance and hidden reality diverge.
terra: God does not disclose the unseen indiscriminately but chooses messengers, clarifying who can carry covered knowledge into speech.

luna: The verse recounts a covenant to make scripture clear to people and not conceal it, then says they cast it behind their backs. It closely stages the choice between disclosure and concealment. | terra: The covenant requires the Book to be made clear and not concealed, directly marking concealment as the breach of revelatory speech.

luna: The source section defines حديث as speech that reaches a hearer. This verse says the disbelievers will wish the earth were leveled with them but will be unable to conceal any حديث from God, joining speech to the limit of concealment. | terra: On judgment day the rejecters cannot conceal any حديث from God, setting an absolute boundary on keeping speech hidden.
terra: The question “Who is truer than God in حديث?” anchors told discourse in divine truth rather than mere human conversation.
terra: Enemies sought to يُضِلُّوكَ, but God revealed the Book and taught the Prophet what he did not know, a direct protection-from-error through disclosure.
terra: God distinguishes messengers whose stories were told to the Prophet from messengers not told before, marking narration's boundary against the still unspoken.
terra: Broken covenant leads to hardened hearts and distortion of revealed words, joining inner corrosion to speech prevented from disclosing truth faithfully.

luna: The verse says the Messenger makes clear much of what the People of the Book had hidden from scripture. It gives the section’s covered-to-revealed movement a concrete scriptural scene. | terra: The Messenger makes clear much that the People of the Book had been concealing, enacting the section's movement from hidden text to public statement.
terra: The revealed Book guides seekers and brings them from darkness into light, completing 5:15's disclosure with the guidance it produces.
terra: The Messenger's duty is clear conveyance, while God knows what people reveal and conceal; public telling stands against complete divine knowledge of both states.
terra: Some matters would trouble the hearers if disclosed, showing that lifting a cover can have a divinely set time and limit.
terra: God commands Jesus to remember His favor and then recounts its concrete forms, closely paralleling the command to speak of the Lord's blessing.

luna: The source section labels ض ل ل branch B002 as hiding or disappearing. Here what the idolaters invented has vanished from them at judgment, a different scene that uses disappearance to expose the absence of their supposed protectors. | terra: What the idolaters fabricated ضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ, vanishes from them, using the section's root in its concrete sense of something once asserted becoming lost from view.
terra: What people had been hiding بَدَا لَهُم, directly naming the moment in which the concealed becomes manifest.
terra: The Prophet is told to state that he does not possess God's treasures or know the unseen, defining the boundary between the messenger and what remains concealed unless revealed.
terra: A leaf, a grain in earth's darkness, and every moist or dry thing are known and held in a clear record, denying that hiddenness means loss.
terra: God takes people during the night, knows what they acquire by day, and raises them again in it, joining nightly concealment to known action and renewed emergence.

luna: The source section says night is a covering and describes finding by sight. In Abraham’s sequence, night covers him and he sees a star; the covered sky becomes the setting for an observed object.

luna: The moon appears in the same sequence, and Abraham says that without his Lord’s guidance he would be among the people astray. The verse joins seeing what appears with the section’s paired ideas of lostness and guidance.

luna: The sequence continues with Abraham seeing the rising sun, the largest of the three lights, then rejecting it when it sets. This contributes the daylight counterpart to the star and moon observations in 6:76–77.

luna: After the star, moon, and sun set, Abraham turns his face to the Creator of the heavens and earth. This resolution completes the neighboring scene of sight and guidance by naming the direction he has found.

luna: The verse says that Moses brought a scripture which people display on pages while concealing much of it. This is a concrete scriptural instance of the section’s movement between what is hidden and what is shown. | terra: People display parts of the revealed Book and conceal much, while the Prophet is commanded to name God as its revealer; telling answers selective hiding.

luna: The verse describes dawn being split, night as repose, and the sun and moon as measures. It makes the cover-to-day transition a created order, not just a shift in visibility. | terra: God splits the dawn and makes night for repose, placing opening light beside settled darkness.
terra: The command distinguishes outward sin from inward sin, applying the manifest-hidden polarity to moral action.
terra: One made alive is given light to walk among people, unlike one enclosed in darkness, joining guidance with becoming perceptible within a crowd.
terra: The Prophet is told to say he does not find in what was revealed a forbidden food beyond those named, showing finding as discernment within received speech.
luna: The verse describes punishment reaching towns at night or while their people rest at midday. It places the section’s two covered and exposed times in one scene of unexpected disclosure.
terra: Satan whispers in order to reveal to Adam and his wife what had been concealed from them of their nakedness, making disclosure itself the temptation's aim.
terra: Their nakedness becomes visible and they begin covering themselves with garden leaves, staging exposure followed immediately by an improvised veil.
terra: The prohibition covers indecencies both outward and inward, repeating the same ethically significant visible-hidden division.
terra: The people of Paradise say they found their Lord's promise true and ask the people of Fire whether they found the same, making future promise present verification.
terra: At fulfillment of the warning, what the rejecters fabricated has vanished from them, another direct use of d-l-l for disappearance rather than wayward travel.

luna: The verse says God covers day with night as it pursues it, and names the sun, moon, and stars as subject to command. This repeats the section’s covering image in a larger account of the alternation of night and day. | terra: Night covers day and pursues it swiftly, giving the section's night-cover a cosmic action.
luna: The verse asks whether a town feels secure from punishment arriving at night while its people sleep. It gives the hidden, sleeping side of the section’s night/day contrast.

luna: The next verse asks whether a town feels secure from punishment arriving at duha while its people play. It supplies the exposed daylight counterpart to the sleeping night in 7:97. | terra: Punishment may come at ضُحًى while a town is playing, using the morning as the exposed public hour rather than the cover of night.
terra: God narrates the news of former towns to the Prophet, carrying vanished communal histories into present warning.
terra: The People of Scripture find the unlettered Messenger written in the Torah and Gospel, turning a preserved textual sign into present recognition.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to relate the account so the hearers may reflect, giving narration the admonitory work of clearing perception.
terra: The Prophet says that if he knew the unseen he would secure much good, defining revelation rather than independent sight as his access to what is covered.
terra: Listeners are commanded to attend silently when the Quran is recited, stating the receptive posture by which revealed speech reaches them.

luna: The source section describes words of admonition polishing the heart. This verse says that when God is mentioned hearts tremble and faith increases when His verses are recited, a specific response to heard revelation. | terra: When God's signs are recited, believers' hearts tremble and their faith increases, a direct Quranic instance of heard admonition acting upon the heart.
terra: Believers are warned not to imitate those who say “we hear” while they do not hear, distinguishing audible arrival from inward reception.
terra: Protection is granted so an outsider may hear the speech of God, making the arrival of revealed words through hearing the ayah's decisive act.
terra: God knows secret counsel and private conversation as Knower of unseen things, so covered speech remains fully present to Him.
terra: God does not let a people stray after guiding them until He makes clear what they must avoid, so clarification guards guidance from loss.
terra: The condemned faces are described as though covered with pieces of dark night, making night-covering a visible human condition.

luna: The source section’s B002 sense is something hidden or gone from sight. At the gathering, what people falsely invented disappears from them, so the verse makes loss visible when each soul faces its deeds. | terra: At judgment every soul encounters what it sent ahead and false objects of worship vanish from their devotees, joining rediscovery of deeds to disappearance of inventions.
terra: While the Prophet recites and people act, not even an atom is hidden from God and all is in a clear record, coupling utterance, perception, and preserved disclosure.

luna: The verse assigns rest to night and sight to day. That is a concrete functional contrast between what the section calls covered and what is open to view. | terra: God makes night for rest and day مُبْصِرًا, giving the day the quality of making sight possible.
terra: The Prophet is told to recite Noah's news to his opponents, making a past confrontation present through voiced report.

luna: The source section links ض ل ل with disappearance. This verse calls its speakers losers because what they invented has strayed from them, portraying false objects of trust as gone when needed. | terra: What the self-wrongers invented has vanished from them, preserving the root's “gone missing” face in an eschatological scene.
terra: Noah is commanded to deny possessing God's treasures or knowing the unseen, preserving the boundary between prophetic telling and unrevealed hidden knowledge.
terra: The account is news of the unseen revealed to the Prophet, which neither he nor his people knew before; hidden history becomes told knowledge.
terra: The reports of the messengers are narrated to steady the Prophet's heart, directly supplying the heart-polishing effect the section gives to admonitory speech.

luna: The section compares its movement from what was unknown to what is told with this address to the Prophet: God relates the best narrative and says he had been among the unaware before it. The story makes revelation the passage from unknowing into recitation. | terra: God narrates the best account to the Prophet, who had previously been unaware of it, exactly tracing the passage from unknown to revealed and told.
luna: Yusuf sees a dream and tells it to his father. This is a specific passage from an inward, unseen experience to narration, matching the section’s move from what is covered to what is said.

luna: The section says the Lord’s favor should be told openly; Jacob instead tells Yusuf not to disclose his dream to his brothers because they may plot against him. The contrast marks a case where keeping what was seen under cover protects the speaker.

luna: The source section notes the secondary word حديث and its relation to what reaches a hearer. This verse says Yusuf will be taught the interpretation of الأحاديث and that God will complete His favor upon him, joining hidden dreams, their interpretation, and bestowed favor.

luna: The section joins concealment, finding, and telling. In Joseph’s story a water-drawer lowers a bucket into the well, announces “good news,” finds a boy, and the caravan then hides him as merchandise; the same scene moves from concealment to discovery and back to concealment. | terra: A water drawer brings Joseph out of the well, recognizes him as good news, and the caravan then conceals him as merchandise: finding and re-covering occur in one scene.

luna: The source section notes that حديث can name more than ordinary speech. In this verse Joseph is established in the land and taught the interpretation of الأحاديث, so the same term covers knowledge whose meaning must be disclosed.

luna: The section describes finding by the senses and reason and moving from concealment to what is exposed. In Joseph’s story, his master is found at the door after a hidden encounter, and the woman’s torn shirt becomes visible evidence.
luna: The verse introduces a witness who says to inspect which side of Joseph’s shirt is torn. It supplies the reasoning test that can turn a concealed event into a known one.
luna: The witness says a tear from behind would show the woman’s accusation is false. This verse gives the physical criterion by which the hidden event can be judged.
luna: The master sees the shirt torn from behind and recognizes the deception. This completes the passage from hidden action to evidence found and then interpreted.
terra: Joseph asks to be mentioned to the king, but the freed prisoner forgets the mention, so failed memory keeps Joseph covered in prison.
terra: After a period the former prisoner remembers and announces that he can report the dream's interpretation, allowing forgotten Joseph to re-enter public speech.
terra: Joseph recognizes his brothers while they do not recognize him, concretely showing a known person remaining invisible within ordinary sight.
terra: Joseph orders the brothers' goods hidden in their baggage so they may recognize them later, supplying the concealment that 12:65 resolves by opening and finding.
terra: The brothers open their baggage and وَجَدُوا their returned goods inside, an exact covered-object-to-found-object movement.
terra: Joseph privately tells his brother “I am your brother” while his identity remains hidden from the others, making disclosure selective before it becomes public.
terra: The brothers themselves define the penalty by the person in whose baggage the cup is found, making discovery of the hidden object decisive.
terra: The bags are searched and the cup is brought out of the brother's container, physically completing concealment, search, and extraction.
terra: Joseph keeps the brothers' accusation within himself and does not reveal it, a deliberate pause between hidden knowledge and later disclosure.
terra: Joseph's question about the brothers' former act prompts recognition, initiating the disclosure of the person who has stood unrecognized before them.
terra: The brothers ask whether he is Joseph and he answers that he is, completing hidden identity with explicit self-naming.

luna: The source section defines finding through the senses. Jacob says he senses Joseph’s scent, إِنِّى لَأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَ, recognizing the absent one through smell before the news arrives. | terra: Jacob says he can detect Joseph's scent before the caravan arrives, extending the section's sensory finding beyond sight.

luna: The source section’s hidden-to-found movement appears when the bearer of good news arrives with Joseph’s shirt: Jacob’s sight returns after it is placed on his face. What was lost to perception becomes visible again through a sign. | terra: When the shirt is placed on Jacob's face, his sight returns, turning an indirect sensory recognition into restored visibility.

luna: The section commands the Prophet to tell of his Lord’s favor. Joseph’s closing prayer names what God gave him and thanks Him for teaching him the interpretation of الأحاديث, combining attributed blessing with the section’s secondary dream-and-event sense.
terra: The events are called news of the unseen revealed to the Prophet while he was absent from the scene, sharply distinguishing witness from revelation.
terra: The prophetic accounts are not a fabricated حديث but confirmation and detailed guidance, defining told history as revelatory rather than invented speech.
terra: God covers day with night in a context of signs made distinct for reflection, supporting the cover-and-recognition relation.

luna: The section makes night a cover and daylight an opening, then moves from what is hidden to what is said. This verse puts concealed speech and public speech beside someone hidden by night and conspicuous by day, showing that both sides of the image are known to God.
terra: The steadfast spend divine provision secretly and openly, another concrete pairing of action under cover and before view.
terra: Hearts find rest in God's remembrance, a gentler account of the inward effect attributed in the section to admonitory conversation.
terra: The Book is sent to the Prophet to bring people from darkness into light, uniting disclosed speech with divine guidance.
terra: Moses tells his people to remember God's favor in rescuing them and names the rescue, showing blessing preserved and made public through narration.
terra: Believers are told to spend God's provision secretly and openly, another concrete act performed under cover and before view.
terra: God gives from what people ask, yet His favors cannot be enumerated, marking how much remains beyond any finite recounting of blessing.
terra: Abraham addresses the Lord who knows what people hide and disclose, making the visible-hidden pair part of prayerful speech.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to proclaim openly what he has been commanded, giving the section's final telling movement an explicit public stance.
terra: God's favors cannot be fully counted, marking a limit on the command to tell blessing without denying the duty to recognize its source.
terra: God knows what people conceal and what they declare, a repeated formula that keeps hiddenness distinct from nonexistence.
terra: The Reminder is sent down so the Prophet may make clear to people what was revealed, making explanation the final stage of reception.

luna: The section’s closing command concerns the favor of the Lord. This verse states that every blessing people have is from Allah, making explicit the attribution that the section asks its reader to voice. | terra: Whatever blessing people have is stated to be from God, supplying the attribution implicit in speaking “of your Lord's blessing.”

luna: The section uses water disappearing into milk as an image of something present but unseen within another substance. This verse describes pure milk emerging from within the animal, a related but distinct image of a drink whose origin lies hidden inside.
terra: One endowed with good provision spends from it secretly and openly, joining bestowed favor with its hidden and manifest expression.
terra: People recognize God's blessing and then deny it, the direct failure to move from a found favor into grateful acknowledgment.

luna: The source section’s B002 dictionary sense includes what has gone missing. Here the partners people invented disappear from them when they surrender to God, making the loss a public exposure of their claims. | terra: On judgment day the false objects that people invented vanish from them, so hidden reality displaces their lost fabrication.
terra: The Holy Spirit brings the Quran from the Lord to steady believers and make it guidance and good news, spelling out what the conveyed word does within its hearers.

luna: The section urges naming the Lord’s favor. This town receives abundant provision from every direction but denies God’s blessings and is made to taste hunger and fear, showing the consequence of refusing to acknowledge favor.
terra: Abraham is grateful for God's favors, and God chooses and guides him to a straight path; favor, acknowledgment, and guidance meet in one description.

luna: The verse makes night dark and day illuminating so people can seek their Lord’s bounty and reckon time. It connects concealment and visibility with the section’s movement from hidden provision to recognition. | terra: The night sign is effaced and the day sign made sight-giving so people can seek bounty and reckon time; obscurity and visibility have distinct work.
terra: A person's record is bound to them and will be brought out on resurrection as an open book, turning stored deeds into visible text.
terra: The person is told to read the disclosed record personally, making the uncovered life speak through its own reader.

luna: The source section’s surah foundations include تَنْهَرْ, not to rebuff the petitioner. This verse uses the same Quranic command toward parents, forbidding harsh rebuff and requiring gracious speech.
terra: When the Prophet recites the Quran, a concealed veil stands between him and those who deny the hereafter, preventing disclosed speech from being received.
terra: The opponents have strayed and therefore cannot find a way, placing loss of direction and inability to find in the same consequence.
luna: The verse repeats the question whether people will be raised in a new creation after becoming bones and fragments, another formulation of the section’s cited denial after disappearance.

luna: The source section defines حديث as speech that reaches people and is then recounted. This verse calls the Quran “this discourse” and addresses the Prophet’s grief if people do not believe it, showing the consequence of a message reaching an unreceptive audience. | terra: The Prophet nearly grieves himself because people do not believe “this حديث,” highlighting the painful gap between revealed telling and failed reception.

luna: The section calls night a covering beneath which things are unseen. These youths are made to sleep in a cave for years, a specific concealment that precedes their awakening. | terra: God covers the sleepers' ears in the cave for years, making concealment operate through hearing itself.

luna: The next verse says God awakens them so they may learn which group can best estimate how long they remained. It completes the concealment with a return to awareness and an attempt to name what passed unseen. | terra: God raises the sleepers in order to make known which party best counted the time, turning covered sleep into disclosed knowledge.
terra: God narrates the sleepers' news in truth, turning their secluded and disputed history into sure revealed knowledge.

luna: The section joins the night cover, exposure to the sun, and being guided or lost. This verse describes the sun turning away from the cave’s people and ends by distinguishing whom God guides from whom He leaves astray. | terra: The sun skirts the cave that conceals the sleepers, and the ayah immediately states that whom God guides is guided and whom He lets stray finds no directing protector.
luna: The youths seem awake though they are sleeping, and their dog lies at the cave entrance. This is a specific difference between what sight suggests and what remains hidden within the cave.

luna: The youths awaken, ask one another how long they have remained, and send one to the city for food while urging discretion. It joins finding provision with the need to keep their hidden state from being exposed. | terra: The awakened sleepers send one companion out discreetly and tell him not to make anyone aware of them, explicitly trying to remain hidden before 18:21's discovery.
luna: The youths fear being discovered and forced back into their former religion. This completes their concealment scene by naming what exposure would mean for them.
terra: God causes the sleepers to be discovered so that their concealed life becomes public evidence for resurrection.
terra: The garden owner is urged to enter his visible prosperity with words attributing power to God, an instructed verbal acknowledgment of favor.
terra: The record is set down and people وَجَدُوا what they did present before them, so deeds once out of sight become readable and found.
terra: Those reminded forget what they sent ahead while covers lie over their hearts and heaviness in their ears, binding forgetting, covering, and refusal of guidance.

luna: The section’s lost-in-water image meets the fish that disappears into the sea as Moses and his companion reach the meeting of the seas; the verse also says they forgot it. This gives disappearance, water, and forgetting one concrete scene. | terra: At the meeting of the two seas the fish takes its way into the water, staging a concrete disappearance whose forgetting is named in 18:63.

luna: The section says a fixed use of ض ل ل carries the sense “forget.” The companion now reports that they forgot the fish and that Satan made him forget to mention it, turning the vanished fish into a spoken recovery of the missed sign. | terra: The servant says he forgot the fish and that it took its way into the sea, bringing forgotten memory and an object vanished in liquid into one scene.

luna: Moses recognizes the fish’s disappearance as the sign they sought and retraces their steps. This continuation completes the cited fish episode by showing how what vanished becomes findable through remembered testimony. | terra: Moses recognizes the lost sign as what they were seeking and retraces the footprints, turning disappearance and forgetting into a search that finds its way back.

luna: The section says وَجَدَ can mean noticing or finding through perception and reason. After returning to the site, Moses وَجَدَ a servant of God endowed with mercy and knowledge, a hidden source of guidance he had not known. | terra: Moses and his servant فَوَجَدَا one of God's servants endowed with mercy and hidden knowledge, beginning a lesson in discovery beyond surface sight.
luna: After finding the knowledgeable servant, Moses asks whether he may follow him and learn from what he has been taught. The verse completes the discovery with an explicit request for guidance.
terra: The servant tells Moses not to ask until he يُحْدِثَ له ذكرا, making later speech the appointed means by which concealed meanings will emerge.

luna: The section labels ض ل ل branch B004 with the dictionary sense “forget.” Moses asks not to be taken to task for what he forgot, a direct example of memory failing in the same narrative as the lost fish.
terra: At the separation the servant promises to tell the interpretation of events Moses could not patiently grasp, moving seen acts into explained meaning.

luna: The section’s covered-to-found movement meets a literal hidden provision: treasure lies beneath a wall for two orphan boys, protected until they mature and can extract it. The explanation identifies the concealed good as mercy from their Lord. | terra: The servant finally states the interpretation of the puzzling acts, completing the sequence from visible event to concealed purpose to narration.
terra: When the Prophet is asked about Dhu al-Qarnayn, he promises to recite a remembrance of him, framing the later acts of finding as narrated knowledge.

luna: The source section describes finding through perception. Dhu al-Qarnayn reaches the setting of the sun and وَجَدَهَا apparently setting in a muddy spring, a narrated sight that makes the perceiver’s standpoint part of what is found. | terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn finds the sun setting and finds a people beside its setting place, a repeated sensory use of وَجَدَ framed by sunlight.

luna: The source section opposes covering with appearing in the sun. At the sunrise, Dhu al-Qarnayn finds a people with no shelter from it; the verse presents exposure to daylight as the boundary opposite concealment. | terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn finds the sun rising upon a people for whom God made no covering from it, joining وَجَدَهَا with complete exposure to the sun.
terra: He finds a people who can scarcely understand speech, pairing physical finding with the boundary at which words fail to reach understanding.
terra: Eyes are under a covering from God's remembrance and ears cannot hear, making concealment a chosen failure of both perception and reception.
terra: Mary takes a screen from her people and the spirit then appears to her as a man, a literal covered space followed by manifestation.

luna: The source section says words reach people by hearing or revelation and describes what is covered. This verse says that even speech made aloud leaves a secret and what is still more hidden, setting a limit on what public telling can expose. | terra: Even if speech is voiced aloud, God knows the secret and what is still more hidden, extending concealment beyond ordinary human hearing.
terra: The question “Has the حديث of Moses come to you?” exemplifies the section's definition of hadith as speech reaching someone through revelation.
terra: Immediately after the revealed “حديث of Moses,” Moses sees a fire, tells his family what he has perceived, and hopes to bring news or find guidance there; sight, telling, and finding converge.
terra: God reveals to Moses's mother what is revealed, placing divine disclosure at the start of the infant's concealment-and-return sequence.
terra: The infant Moses is placed in a chest and cast into the river to be taken by an enemy, a concealed child carried into an unknowing finder's hands.
terra: Moses's sister guides the household to a nurse, God returns him to his mother, and later brings him out of distress; hidden identity and guidance restore what was lost.
terra: God “does not go astray and does not forget,” placing the section's two senses of d-l-l at a deliberate divine limit.
terra: Human beings come from earth, return into it, and are brought out from it again, explicitly denying that burial is final disappearance.

luna: The source section glosses the root of ضحى as coming out into the sun and open view. Moses chooses ضُحًى for the people’s public gathering, placing the contest in daylight where it can be seen. | terra: Moses chooses ضُحًى and the gathering of all the people, so the encounter occurs in the openly visible morning developed in the section.
terra: God says He narrates reports of what preceded and has given the Prophet a remembrance, making the hidden past into present admonition.
terra: The Arabic Quran varies warnings so that it may يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا, linking the h-d-th root to speech bringing remembrance into being.
luna: The section’s secondary sense of ض ل ل is forgetting. This verse says Adam had previously been given a command but forgot it, showing a forgotten instruction rather than a lost path.
terra: Adam is promised that in the garden he will not تَضْحَىٰ, be exposed to the sun; this negative use clarifies the dictionary sense of going out into sunlight.
terra: After eating from the tree, Adam and his wife's nakedness becomes visible and they patch leaves over themselves, repeating the exact uncovering-and-covering movement.
terra: Whoever follows divine guidance will neither يَضِلُّ nor suffer, stating the lasting result of the guidance that follows dāll in 93:7.
terra: Each newly given reminder is heard while the people play, showing revealed speech arriving at ears but failing to open attention.
terra: God knows speech spoken aloud and what people conceal, covering both audible expression and its unvoiced counterpart.
terra: God will raise those in graves, a direct doctrinal boundary against bodies being irretrievably lost in earth.
terra: The ayah says that eyes are not what go blind but hearts within breasts, setting a boundary between surface visibility and genuine perception.
terra: Those given knowledge recognize the revelation as truth, believe it, and their hearts humbly submit, showing disclosed speech polishing inward perception.
terra: Destroyed peoples are made أَحَادِيثَ, so vanished communities remain present as stories told by later mouths.
luna: The verse asks whether people will be raised after dying and becoming dust and bones. It repeats the same bodily-disappearance challenge as the section’s 32:10 passage.
luna: The verse says that tongues, hands, and feet will testify to what people did. It repeats the body-as-witness image and makes private actions publicly known.
terra: The command not to reveal hidden adornment even guards against a footfall that would make it known, showing concealment undone through hearing.
terra: The thirsty person reaches the apparent water and finds nothing, then وَجَدَ اللَّهَ; the ayah tests sensory finding against what is truly there.

luna: The section says night hides what is underneath its cover. This sea is layered in darkness, and a person can scarcely see his own hand; it gives a concrete scene of sight failing under overlapping cover. | terra: Layered sea, wave, cloud, and darkness make even one's hand nearly invisible; without God's light there is no light, the full negative of morning disclosure.

luna: The source section names straying from the way as the root’s familiar sense. Here those making false comparisons are lost and cannot find a way, making the loss a failure to locate a path. | terra: The opponents have strayed and cannot find a path, a concise inverse of being found in a state of dalal and then guided.

luna: The verse calls night a garment and sleep rest, then makes day a time of spreading out. It links the source section’s covering image to the different activity revealed in daylight. | terra: God makes night a garment and sleep a repose, then makes day a rising forth, explicitly staging cover followed by emergence.

luna: The source section’s dictionary image is water disappearing into milk. This verse gives the boundary case of two waters meeting while a barrier keeps them apart, clarifying the difference between mixture and separation.
terra: Those reminded by God's signs do not respond as deaf and blind, defining true reception as awakened hearing and sight.
terra: Each newly given reminder is met by turning away, a precise contrast to admonitory حديث polishing a receptive heart.
terra: Moses describes his earlier act as done while he was among the ضَالِّينَ, placing a confessed former state immediately before divine commissioning.
terra: Moses says his Lord then granted judgment and made him a messenger, completing 26:20's movement from error or unawareness into guided speech.
terra: The trustworthy Spirit brings the revelation down, identifying the messenger by which concealed divine speech reaches the human sphere.
terra: The revelation descends upon the Prophet's heart so that he may warn, joining inward reception to outward address.
terra: The disclosure is in a clear Arabic tongue, giving audible and intelligible form to what descended upon the heart.
terra: Moses tells his family that he perceives a fire and may bring them news or a burning brand, turning distant sight into the prospect of reported knowledge.
terra: Solomon voices a prayer to be enabled to thank the favor bestowed on him and his parents, exemplifying blessing deliberately brought into speech.
terra: The hoopoe says it has encompassed what Solomon does not know and has brought sure news, moving unseen knowledge into an audible report.
terra: The hoopoe's وَجَدتُّ report identifies the queen, her throne, and her rule, so an act of finding becomes the content of telling.

luna: The source section says وَجَدَ can mean noticing through the senses. The hoopoe reports that he found the queen and her people prostrating to the sun, making an observed scene the basis of a message that exposes what had been hidden from Solomon. | terra: The hoopoe continues “I found her and her people” and reports their sun worship, carrying the discovered scene fully into speech.
terra: God is described as bringing out الْخَبْءَ, the hidden thing in heaven and earth, while knowing all that people conceal and reveal.

luna: The section moves from a hidden or missed thing to a found blessing that is spoken of. Solomon sees the distant throne placed before him and calls it a favor from his Lord, explicitly turning discovery into recognition of divine favor. | terra: When the throne is made present, Solomon openly identifies it as his Lord's favor and a test of gratitude, enacting speech about a newly manifested gift.

luna: The verse asks whether people see that night was made for rest and day for sight. It repeats the section’s contrast between what is hidden in night and what becomes visible by day. | terra: Night is made for rest and day sight-giving, a compact functional parallel to night covering and duha revealing.
terra: Moses's mother receives revelation to cast the child into the river and a promise that God will return him, beginning a hidden-child-to-restoration sequence.
terra: Pharaoh's household picks the concealed infant from the river, a discovery whose true identity remains unknown to the finders.
terra: Moses's mother nearly discloses his identity, but God steadies her heart so the secret remains covered for a time.
terra: Moses's sister watches him from a distance while his captors remain unaware of her, staging observation hidden within a crowd.
terra: The sister offers to guide the household to carers while concealing that she is guiding them back to Moses's own family.
terra: God returns Moses to his mother so she will know the promise is true, ending concealed separation in recognition and knowledge.

luna: The source section’s dictionary gloss calls a town’s outward side its exposed edge. A man runs from the far end of Moses’s city with a warning, a specific scene of a voice emerging from the city’s edge into public view. | terra: A man comes running from the city's farthest edge and discloses the chiefs' hidden plot to Moses, linking the section's “outward side of a town” detail to warning speech.

luna: The section describes وَجَدَ as noticing through perception. Moses finds two women holding their flock back from the watering crowd, notices their need, and asks what is happening. | terra: Moses finds a crowd watering and notices two women held back from it, a gaze that singles out otherwise overlooked people within the crowd.
luna: After Moses waters their flock, he withdraws to shade and asks his Lord for whatever good He sends. The continuation connects a found need and a response with asking for provision.

luna: A woman comes to Moses with her father’s invitation and the offer of a reward for watering the flock. The good deed that began with noticing need is made known through a spoken message and returned provision.
terra: Moses perceives a fire from the side of the mount and tells his family he may bring news or fire, another sensory finding poised to become speech.
terra: At the fire Moses is called from the tree in the blessed ground, completing the preceding perception with a revelatory voice.
terra: The Prophet was not present when Moses received the command, so the narrated scene marks knowledge supplied without ordinary witnessing.
terra: Generations and distance separate the Prophet from Midian, sharpening the hidden historical gap that revelation crosses.
terra: The Prophet was not beside the mount but is sent as mercy to warn, completing absence from the event with public speech about it.
terra: The Lord knows what breasts conceal and what people reveal, setting inward covering beside outward manifestation.
terra: The thought experiment of perpetual night asks who besides God could bring light, making emergence from cover depend wholly on Him.
terra: The matching thought experiment asks who could bring night for rest if day were perpetual, preserving the purpose of the cover as well as its lifting.
terra: God's mercy supplies both resting night and sight-giving day, completing the visible-hidden pair with their human uses.

luna: The source section’s B002 sense is hiddenness or disappearance. This verse says the truth becomes clear and the inventions they relied on vanish, placing disclosure beside the disappearance. | terra: When witnesses are summoned and proof demanded, the fabricated partners vanish from their worshippers, making failed finding expose the false claim.
terra: Qarun attributes his wealth to his own knowledge, reversing Solomon's open recognition that a manifested gift is favor from his Lord.
terra: People know only the outward surface of worldly life while remaining heedless of the hereafter, showing manifest knowledge that still conceals the larger reality.
terra: Idle حديث is purchased to mislead people from God's way, reversing the section's حديث that discloses, admonishes, and guides.
terra: God's favors are explicitly ظَاهِرَةً وَبَاطِنَةً, giving the blessing to be told in 93:11 both its manifest and hidden layers.

luna: The source section labels ض ل ل branch B002 as hiding and disappearing, and cites this wording: ضَلَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ. Here resurrection-deniers imagine becoming lost in the earth, making bodily disappearance the premise of their denial. | terra: The deniers use ضَلَلْنَا for bodies disappearing into earth, making concrete the section's secondary sense of dalal as being present yet lost from sight.
terra: Believers are told to remember God's favor when unseen forces turned back attacking armies, making hidden aid a narrated blessing.
terra: Whether something is displayed or concealed, God encompasses it in knowledge, denying that cover removes a thing from perception altogether.
terra: No atom in heaven or earth is hidden from God and all is in a clear record, another precise denial that invisibility means loss.

luna: The section cites people asking whether they will be created anew after disappearing into the earth. This verse repeats the resurrection denial in different words: after being torn apart, they ask whether they will be in a new creation.
terra: Solomon's death remains hidden from the jinn until the staff gives way and his fall makes it clear, a physical fact moving from concealment to discovery.
terra: A people scattered and removed from sight are made أَحَادِيثَ, preserving them precisely by turning them into narrated accounts.
terra: The Prophet says that if he strays it is his own loss, but if he is guided it is through what his Lord reveals; revelation is the audible source of guidance.
terra: People are commanded to remember God's favor and asked whether any creator besides Him provides for them, joining recollection of blessing to public attribution of its source.
terra: The Prophet cannot make those in graves hear, marking the human limit of speech reaching what the earth covers.
terra: Those who recite the Book also spend provision secretly and openly, placing heard or spoken revelation beside both modes of action.

luna: The source section’s dictionary gloss describes the exposed side of a town; the connection here is spatial rather than lexical. A man comes running from the farthest part of the city to urge his people to follow the messengers, so the city edge becomes the point from which a public message emerges. | terra: A man comes running from the city's farthest edge and publicly urges his people to follow the messengers, turning the peripheral side of town into a place of proclamation.

luna: The verse says daylight is stripped from night and people are suddenly in darkness. This makes the boundary between appearing and being covered an action, matching the section’s movement between hidden and exposed. | terra: Day is stripped away and people are suddenly in darkness, showing visibility itself as a layer that can be removed.
terra: A blast sounds and the dead rush from their graves to their Lord, turning concealed bodies into an openly moving multitude.
luna: The verse says that mouths are sealed while hands speak and feet testify to what people did. It is a specific image of hidden deeds becoming a spoken record.
terra: The Prophet is comforted that God knows what opponents conceal and reveal, so hostile speech and its hidden source are both already perceived.
luna: The verse asks who can revive bones after they have decayed. It makes the bodily disappearance in the section’s resurrection example a specific image of bones losing their form.
luna: The answer is that the One who created the bones the first time will revive them. This completes the challenge in 36:78 with the reversal from decay to restoration.
luna: The verse asks whether people will be resurrected after they die and become dust and bones, a further direct formulation of the denial the section quotes.
terra: The condemned وَجَدُوا their fathers ضَالِّينَ, bringing “finding” and “astray” together while showing discovery that merely perpetuates inherited error.
terra: God says وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِرًا of Job, illustrating intellectual or evaluative finding rather than the section's sensory finding.

luna: The verse describes God wrapping night over day and day over night. Its reversible covering gives the section’s night-and-day opposition a recurring, two-way movement. | terra: Night is wrapped over day and day over night, portraying concealment and disclosure as reciprocal coverings.
terra: Those who listen to speech and follow its best are the ones God guides, coupling audible words with the guidance that follows finding.
terra: A breast opened to Islam follows light from the Lord, while hardened hearts resist remembrance; openness and light oppose the unpolished heart.

luna: The source section gives ح د ث a sense of bringing out and describes counsel as polishing hearts. This verse calls revelation أَحْسَنَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ and says it makes hearts soften at remembrance, a direct meeting of the word’s speech sense with its effect on the heart. | terra: God sends down أَحْسَنَ الْحَدِيثِ and its admonition makes skins tremble and then hearts soften, the Quranic counterpart to speech polishing a heart.
terra: God knows the stealthy glance and what breasts conceal, making even the nearly invisible act perceptible to divine knowledge.
terra: Night is made for rest and day for seeing, repeating the image as a provision people are asked to recognize.

luna: The source section’s B002 gloss covers disappearance. Those questioned about their former partners answer that they have gone away from them, a concrete case of what was relied on becoming absent. | terra: The condemned answer that the objects they invoked have vanished from them, a first-person acknowledgment of the root's disappearance sense.
terra: As in 4:164, some messengers have been narrated to the Prophet and others have not, preserving both the disclosed account and what remains covered.
terra: The hearers claim covers over hearts, heaviness in ears, and a veil between themselves and the Prophet, the opposite of speech reaching and polishing a heart.

luna: On the Day of Judgment, people’s hearing, sight, and skins testify against them. This is a specific reversal of the section’s movement from hidden experience to spoken account: the body itself discloses what its owner concealed.
luna: The people ask their skins why they testified, and the skins answer that God made them speak. This completes 41:20 by naming the source of the disclosure.
terra: People could not hide from their own hearing, sight, and skins bearing witness, so the senses that once received actions become their narrators.
terra: The rejecters tell one another not to listen to the Quran and to drown it in noise, deliberately preventing revelation from reaching the ear as meaningful speech.
terra: God's speech reaches a human by revelation, from behind a veil, or through a messenger, exactly mapping hearing and revelation across a boundary of concealment.
terra: The Prophet did not know the Book or faith, then revelation was made a light by which God guides; it directly fills out “found unaware, then guided.”
terra: Secret speech and private counsel are heard and recorded, so words do not cease to exist merely because human ears are excluded.
terra: God sends the clarifying Book down during a blessed night as warning, making the night-cover itself the setting from which revelation emerges.

luna: The source section says speech received through revelation is called حديث. This verse identifies the recited signs as God’s and asks what discourse people will believe after His signs, tying revelation to a hearer’s response. | terra: After God's signs are recited, the question asks what حديث people will believe after God and His signs, setting revealed discourse as the limit beyond which substitute speech cannot guide.
terra: One led astray despite knowledge has hearing and heart sealed and sight veiled, reversing the section's finding, guidance, and lifting of cover.
terra: A group of jinn listens to the Quran, tells one another to attend, then returns to warn its people; heard revelation becomes retold warning.
terra: The jinn identify what they heard as a Book guiding to truth and a straight path, stating the guidance produced by the speech in 46:29.
terra: God promises never to let the slain believers' deeds be lost, setting a divine boundary against the d-l-l sense of disappearance.
terra: The question about pondering the Quran locates locks upon hearts, presenting speech whose clarifying work is stopped by an inner closure.
terra: Those with diseased hearts suppose God will not bring out their concealed rancor, echoing the image of what is inwardly covered being exposed.
terra: God could show the hypocrites so the Prophet would recognize them by marks, and their hidden state is already recognizable in the tone of speech.

luna: The verse asks whether people will return after dying and becoming dust. Like the section’s 32:10 example, bodily disappearance into earth is used to challenge resurrection. | terra: The deniers ask whether return is possible after death and becoming dust; 50:4 answers this disappearance by affirming that God knows what earth diminishes.

luna: The verse answers the disappearance claim by saying God knows what the earth diminishes of them and has a preserving record. It adds the counterpoint that what is hidden from human view is not lost to God.
luna: Each person arrives with a driver and a witness. This verse sets up the judgment scene that continues with the cover removed and sight made sharp in 50:22.

luna: The verse says the cover is removed and sight becomes sharp. It directly joins uncovering to recovered vision, matching the section’s hidden-to-found movement. | terra: The heedless person's covering is removed and sight becomes sharp, giving the image an eschatological instance of cover lifted into perception.
terra: The revelation is a reminder for one with a receptive heart who listens as a witness, matching speech that reaches the ear and works upon the heart.

luna: The section’s surrounding surah says not to rebuff the asker. This verse states that a due share of wealth belongs to the asker and the deprived, turning hidden generosity into an explicit right.
terra: The حديث of Abraham's honored guests is presented as something that has reached the addressee, matching the named dictionary sense exactly.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to remind, and “by your Lord's blessing” he is neither soothsayer nor madman; favor supports the stance of open proclamation.

luna: The section notes the root’s path-lost sense beside its “hidden and gone” sense. This verse says the Prophet’s companion has neither strayed nor erred, setting a clear boundary against reading 93:7 as moral deviation. | terra: The oath denies that “your companion” has strayed, illuminating 93:7 by distinguishing the Prophet's earlier dāll state from his present truthful mission.
terra: After 53:2 denies that the Prophet has strayed, this ayah states that his speech is not from desire, beginning the account of what his telling now is.
terra: The Prophet's utterance is identified as revelation, completing the contrast in 53:2 between being called astray and conveying disclosed guidance.
terra: People emerge from graves with lowered eyes, making the concealed dead suddenly visible as a spread multitude.
luna: The two seas are released and meet, echoing the source section’s image of one liquid entering another; the next verse’s barrier makes the contrast explicit.
luna: The neighboring verse supplies the boundary between the two meeting seas: a barrier they do not cross. It completes the contrast with the source section’s water that disappears within milk.
luna: The verse quotes people asking whether they will be resurrected after dying and becoming dust and bones. It repeats the same challenge while placing it in a passage that answers it.
terra: The hearers are challenged for treating “this حديث” with disdain, contrasting the revealed word's arrival with a response that suppresses its worth.

luna: The section describes blessings as both apparent and hidden. This verse applies the paired terms to God as the Manifest and the Hidden, shifting the visible/hidden distinction from the gift to its giver. | terra: God is named both the Manifest and the Hidden, placing the section's visible-hidden polarity in a single divine description.

luna: The section’s hadith gloss includes counseling hearts until they are polished. This verse asks whether believers’ hearts have become humble to God’s remembrance and revealed truth, contrasting a softened heart with one that has grown hard.
terra: God has counted deeds that people forgot and will tell them what they did, so forgotten acts remain preserved for later narration.
terra: God is present with every private conversation and will later tell its speakers what they did, joining hidden speech to eventual disclosure.
terra: Secretly conveying affection is set beside God's knowledge of what is concealed and declared, making private communication itself visible to Him.
terra: God knows what is concealed and declared as well as what lies within breasts, repeating the image's outer and inner planes of visibility.
terra: God may يُحْدِثُ after a divorce some new matter, preserving the h-d-th root's sense of bringing something previously absent into being.
terra: A messenger recites God's clear signs in order to bring believers from darkness into light, so spoken revelation performs the section's uncovering.

luna: The source section defines حديث as speech that reaches a hearer and حَدَّثَ as bringing something out. This verse calls a confidence حديث, then narrates its disclosure to another wife, God making it known to the Prophet, and his revealing part of it. | terra: A حديث is confided, divulged, disclosed by God, and partly made known by the Prophet; the whole ayah stages speech moving from secrecy to disclosure.
terra: The people of the Fire admit that listening or reasoning would have saved them, identifying failed reception of warning as their decisive loss.
terra: Whether speech is kept secret or voiced aloud, God knows what lies within breasts; neither form of saying escapes the divine hearing.
terra: The phrase “by your Lord's blessing” publicly rejects the charge of madness against the Prophet, making divine favor part of his spoken vindication.
terra: When the owners see their ruined garden they first say they are ضَالُّونَ, using the root for failing to recognize the place they are looking at.
terra: On the day people are presented, no hidden thing remains hidden, giving the section's lifting of the cover its absolute boundary.
terra: The person given the record openly calls others to read it, turning the unveiled life of 69:18 into a narrated document.
luna: The verse says that the faithful keep a known share in their wealth, a detail that makes provision answerable to people in need rather than remaining solely with its holder.
luna: The next verse identifies the recipients as the asker and the deprived, directly connecting the section’s treatment of a petitioner with a claim on provision.
terra: Noah's people put fingers in ears and wrap themselves in garments to avoid his call, physically blocking the speech that should reach and uncover.
terra: Noah says he proclaimed openly and also spoke privately, explicitly setting public telling beside concealed address.
terra: The Prophet is told that jinn listened and then reported the wondrous Quran, another complete reception-to-telling movement.
terra: The jinn reach toward heaven and find it newly filled with guards and flames, a sensory discovery of a realm whose changed state had been hidden from them.
terra: God knows the unseen and does not disclose His unseen to anyone, stating the veil before the exception in 72:27.
terra: A chosen messenger is the exception to concealed unseen knowledge, establishing revelation as authorized disclosure.
terra: The guarded disclosure ensures that the messengers have conveyed their Lord's messages, carrying hidden knowledge through to public delivery.
terra: The Prophet is addressed as the one wrapped up, placing him literally beneath a cover before the ensuing night recitation.
terra: The wrapped Prophet is commanded to stand through the night, moving from covered rest into alert reception.
terra: He is commanded to recite the Quran in measured form, completing the movement from wrapping and night into articulated revelation.
terra: The Prophet is addressed as the one wrapped in a covering, giving the image a human bearer immediately before the command to speak publicly.
terra: The wrapped Prophet is commanded to rise and warn, enacting movement from covering in 74:1 into proclamation.
terra: After the covered Prophet is told to rise and warn, he is commanded to magnify his Lord, specifying the God-directed content of the public utterance.
terra: The retreating night marks the withdrawal of the cover before the morning appears in the next ayah.
terra: The morning when it shines gives the emergence into visibility that completes 74:33's departing night.
terra: The human being supposes that God will not gather the bones, expressing bodily disappearance as a mistaken conclusion.
terra: God answers that He can restore even fingertips, setting exact reconstitution against the supposed loss in 75:3.
terra: The human being is informed that day of what was sent ahead and left behind, turning a completed but hidden life into narrated knowledge.
terra: God takes responsibility for gathering the revelation and its recitation, securing the words before they are publicly voiced.
terra: Once God recites the revelation, the Prophet is told to follow its recitation, tracing speech from divine delivery into human reception.
terra: God also takes responsibility for its clarification, completing collection and recitation with the making-clear central to this image.
terra: The question asks what حديث after this revelation the rejecters will believe, exposing refusal at the final point where clarifying speech has reached them.

luna: The source section calls night a covering. This verse names the night as لباس, a garment, making the concealing function explicit. | terra: Night is made a garment, the Quran's most concrete parallel to the section's opening statement that night is a cover.

luna: The next verse makes day a means of livelihood, supplying the exposed, active counterpart to the night garment in 78:10. | terra: Day is made for livelihood, giving the uncovered interval in 78:10-11 its outward human work.

luna: The source section defines حديث as speech that reaches through hearing or revelation. This narrative begins by asking whether the report of Moses has reached the listener, then recounts a scene of divine address. | terra: The question whether Moses's حديث has reached the Prophet makes arrival through revealed hearing the point of the wording.

luna: The source section explains ضحى as emergence into open sunlight. This verse says God darkened the night and brought out its ضُحَىٰ, a direct image of what was covered becoming visible. | terra: God darkens the night and أَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا, literally bringing its morning brightness out after concealment.

luna: The verse says the written records are spread open. It gives a concrete disclosure of what had been preserved out of sight. | terra: The records are spread open, making what was stored and closed available to sight.

luna: The next verse says each soul will know what it has brought. This completes the opened-record scene with recognition of what was hidden in one’s own deeds. | terra: After the records are opened, every soul knows what it has brought, giving disclosure its corresponding act of recognition.
terra: The night is sworn by as it withdraws, an alternate formulation of the cover beginning to lift.
terra: The dawn is sworn by as it breathes, completing 81:17 with light's gradual emergence.
terra: The Prophet has seen the messenger on the clear horizon, supplying the act of visible perception before 81:24 says he does not withhold the unseen.
terra: The Prophet does not withhold the unseen, so what God discloses is not kept under a cover but conveyed.

luna: The verse says graves are overturned, exposing what they held. This is a direct scene of what was covered in burial being brought into view. | terra: The graves are overturned, making the place of bodily concealment openly yield what it held.
luna: The next verse says each soul will know what it sent ahead and left behind, completing the grave-opening scene with disclosure of its record.

luna: The source section says the hadith root can describe polishing a heart with admonitions. This verse says deeds have rusted over hearts, the contrary condition that makes the image of polishing perceptible. | terra: A rust-like covering has accumulated on hearts through deeds, directly opposing the section's image of admonition polishing a heart clean.

luna: The earth casts out what is within it and empties itself, a direct counterpart to the section’s hidden material becoming exposed. | terra: The earth casts out what is inside it and becomes empty, a direct reversal of bodies disappearing into the ground in 32:10.
luna: The neighboring verse says the earth listens to and obeys its Lord. It completes the image of its disclosure with the source of its response.
terra: The حديث of the armies is asked about as revelation that reaches the listener from a past otherwise unseen.

luna: The section centers what is concealed becoming known. This verse says hidden things will be tested or exposed, making disclosure itself the event of judgment. | terra: The day when secrets are tested and exposed gives the section's hidden interior a decisive moment of disclosure.
terra: God promises to make the Prophet recite so that he will not forget, joining received speech to the preservation of what could vanish from memory.
terra: The recitation promise is grounded in God's knowledge of what is public and what is hidden, joining memory, speech, and the visible-hidden pair.

luna: The source section describes speech as what reaches a hearer. This verse opens by asking whether the account of the overwhelming event has reached the Prophet, moving an unseen future event into recitation. | terra: The حديث of the Overwhelming is posed as news that has reached the Prophet, joining future unseen event and present telling.
terra: The oath by dawn supplies the revealing edge of the night whose passing is named in 89:4.
terra: The oath by night as it passes presents the cover in the act of withdrawal toward 89:1's dawn.
terra: The oath by the sun and ضُحَاهَا ties duha directly to the sun's spreading brightness.

luna: The source section opposes what is covered to what comes into view. This oath describes the day as it reveals the sun, a close parallel to the image’s emergence into light. | terra: The day is sworn by when it جَلَّاهَا, revealing the sun, a direct cosmic image of brightness making visible.

luna: The next oath describes night as it covers the sun, completing the day-and-night reversal that the section reads through concealment and appearance. | terra: The night is sworn by when it covers the sun, providing the exact concealment paired with 91:3's unveiling.

luna: The source section’s sword and heart-polishing image implies cleansing what has accumulated. This verse says the person who purifies the soul succeeds, giving purification a concrete spiritual outcome.
luna: The next verse says the person who buries or corrupts the soul fails. It supplies the direct opposite of purification and echoes the section’s hidden-versus-brought-into-view boundary.

luna: The source section calls night a covering beneath which things are unseen. This oath names the night when it covers, directly staging that side of the image. | terra: The night is sworn by when it covers, stating the section's night-as-cover image in the verb يَغْشَىٰ.

luna: The verse immediately sets out the day as it appears, giving the open and visible counterpart to the source section’s covered night. | terra: The day is sworn by when it becomes manifest, completing 92:1's passage from covering to disclosure.
luna: The same Lord addresses the Prophet and says that He raised his mention. This is a specific public-mention counterpart to the section’s command that the Prophet tell of his Lord’s favor.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to recite in his Lord's name, making received knowledge cross immediately into spoken proclamation.
